newsitem.title: INDIA: East India Hotels raises room tariffs.
newsitem.headline: East India Hotels raises room tariffs.

text.p: Leading Indian hospitality firm East India Hotels said on Tuesday it hiked its room tariffs by an average 7-8 percent in dollar terms and by an average 17-18 percent in rupee terms.
The new rates are effective from October 1.
East India is the flagship of the Oberoi group. It operates hotels under the Oberoi and Trident brands.
Shib Sanker Mukherji, vice president (finance), told Reuters the firm had hiked dollar tariffs by 7.0 percent and rupee tariffs by 13 percent for The Oberoi hotel in Bombay.
Rupee tariffs were raised by 17 percent and dollar rates by around 7-8 percent for The Oberoi Towers hotel -- which is also located in Bombay.
In New Delhi, room rates for The Oberoi were up by 9.0 percent in dollar terms and almost 25 percent in rupee terms, Mukherji said.
He said the company's turnover during April-August was up 18 percent over the first five months of 1995/96. Gross operating profit rose 18.5 percent during the first five months over the year ago.
"September is likely to improve the situation further," Mukherji said.
